newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Mitsubishi Chemical to raise market share.
newsitem.headline: Mitsubishi Chemical to raise market share.

text.p: Mitsubishi Chemical Corp (MCC) aims to capture about 20 percent of the global market for data storage media by 1999, helped by output from its newly opened Singapore production plant, MCC president Akira Miura said on Friday.
"We aim to corner 20 percent of the world's market for data storage media," he said, at the opening of the new manufacturing plant in Singapore, run by Mitsubishi Chemical Infornics (MCI)
MCI is a wholly-owned unit of Mitsubishi Chemical Singapore. Miura said Mitsubishi would invest actively in manufacturing outside of Japan for hard disk media and compact discs.
The new Singapore $450 million facility, the second phase of three phases, lays the foundation for Mitsubishi's strategic global focus on the information and electronic business, he said.
Yoshimitsu Kobayashi, general manager of information storage products, told reporters at a briefing Mitsubishi's hard disk media made up some nine to 10 percent of worldwide capacity.
The aim was to increase market share for recordable compact discs (CDR) and also rewritable compact discs (CDRW), he said.
With the new production capacity, MCC will be able to achieve 35 million hard disks and 70 million CDR and CDRW discs annually in a few years, more than double its present capacity.
All three products would in total eventually comprise 20 percent of global supply, Kobayashi said.
He added the target for CDRW's output was 30 percent.
Studies are now being carried out on digital video discs, the latest in multimedia technology, but a decision to produce the item here has not been made yet, he said.
Mitsubishi's main export customers are Quantum Corp of the U.S. and Verbatim, a unit of MCC.
A third phase of production in Singapore, currently under construction, will produce organic photo conductor (OPC) drums used in photocopy machines and laser printers.
That investment of S$40 million brings MCI's investment here to S$560 million.
Its initial investment of S$20 million in a small CDR plant in Singapore started production two years ago.
Official figures show Singapore is the world's largest producer of hard disk drives and ships some 42 percent of overall output. It also exports about 10 percent of hard disk media.
